skill.name: api-spectral
skill.description: Guides Spectral linting for OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and Arazzo specifications using OWASP-focused rules, custom policies, reports, and CI workflows.
skill.summary: Validate API specifications against security, design, and governance rules with Spectral.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, defensive examples, fixed local file reads, or reference URLs. Confirmed risks include unverified remote downloads, mutable CI dependencies, token exposure, and fail-open scanner steps. These supply-chain and enforcement weaknesses require remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: The CI template pipes a mutable remote installer directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Install tfsec from a pinned release and verify its checksum or signature before execution.

remediation.issue: Remote scripts, rulesets, packages, and actions are not pinned to immutable versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions to commit SHAs, packages to reviewed versions, and downloads to immutable commits with integrity verification.

remediation.issue: A mutable third-party action receives GITHUB_TOKEN with workflow permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the action, reduce job permissions, and pass the token only when the documented feature requires it.

remediation.issue: Scanner commands suppress errors and some results do not enforce a failure threshold.
remediation.suggestion: Separate tool errors from findings, validate every report, and fail the workflow when scans fail or exceed policy.

Create a `.spectral.yaml` ruleset extending built-in security rules:
- `spectral:oas` - OpenAPI v2/v3.x security and best practices
- Use `error` severity for critical security issues (authentication, HTTPS)
- Use `warn` for recommended practices and information disclosure risks
- Use `info` for style guide compliance and documentation completeness
- `junit` - JUnit XML for test reporting platforms
For complete OWASP API Security Top 10 rule mappings, see `references/owasp_api_mappings.md`.
- `references/custom_rules_guide.md` - Complete rule authoring guide with functions
- `assets/rule-templates/` - Reusable rule templates for common security patterns
For complete CI/CD integration examples, see `scripts/ci_integration_examples/`.
For complete custom function development guide, see `references/custom_functions.md`.
- `parse_spectral_results.py` - Parse Spectral JSON output and generate security reports with OWASP
- `generate_remediation.py` - Generate remediation guidance based on Spectral findings
- `compare_spectral_results.py` - Compare two Spectral scans to track remediation progress
- `aggregate_api_findings.py` - Aggregate findings across multiple API specifications
- `spectral_ci.sh` - CI/CD integration wrapper with exit code handling
- `generate_pr_comments.py` - Convert Spectral findings to PR review comments
- `owasp_api_mappings.md` - Complete OWASP API Security Top 10 rule mappings
- `ruleset_patterns.md` - Reusable ruleset patterns for common security scenarios
- `spectral-owasp.yaml` - Comprehensive OWASP API Security Top 10 ruleset
- Start with `error` severity only: `spectral lint --fail-severity error`
- Use `overrides` section in ruleset to exclude specific paths
- Use `--verbose` flag to see which rules are being applied
- Lint specific paths only: `spectral lint api-spec.yaml --ignore-paths "components/examples"`
- Use `--skip-rules` to disable expensive rules temporarily
- Use `--fail-severity` to control when builds should fail
- `compare_spectral_results.py` - Compare two Spectral scans to track remediation progress

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned CI dependencies execute mutable upstream code
semantic_findings.description: The templates install unversioned packages and run actions from mutable tags, including a master branch. Upstream compromise can change code executed by CI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files directly show unversioned package installation, mutable action tags, and aquasecurity/trivy-action@master in executable workflow steps.

semantic_findings.title: Security pipeline can pass after scanner failures
semantic_findings.description: Several scanner commands suppress failures, while later checks omit or only warn on some results. Tool errors and detected vulnerabilities can leave the workflow successful.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The templates explicitly use continue-on-error or || true, and the npm audit output is not included in the dependency failure check.

critical_findings.title: Hardcoded URL
critical_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mutable upstream URL supplies an installer directly to bash on the same line. A compromised branch or connection can produce arbitrary CI code execution.

critical_findings.title: Pipe to shell pattern
critical_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template pipes an unverified installer from a mutable upstream branch directly into bash. This creates a direct supply-chain remote code execution path in CI.

high_findings.title: Git platform tokens

content.value_statement: Inconsistent API definitions can hide security and governance defects. This skill guides Spectral configuration, OWASP-focused linting, custom rules, reporting, and CI integration.
actual_capabilities: Guides Spectral linting for OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and Arazzo specifications.
Provides OWASP-focused rules and mappings for API specification reviews.
Explains custom Spectral rules, JSONPath targets, functions, and severity levels.
Supplies GitHub Actions and general CI workflow templates.
Shows report generation, result comparison, and staged-file validation patterns.
limitations: Spectral validates specifications, not deployed API behavior or runtime authorization.
The skill requires Spectral and Node.js; some examples also require Docker, Git, jq, or Python.
Several scripts and reference files named in SKILL.md are not included in this package.
Custom rules can produce false positives and require review against organizational policy.

use_cases.title: Review an API specification
use_cases.description: Find missing security schemes, insecure servers, exposed data patterns, and incomplete responses before implementation.

use_cases.title: Create governance rules
use_cases.description: Define organization-specific Spectral checks and map findings to OWASP API Security categories.

use_cases.title: Add CI enforcement
use_cases.description: Integrate specification linting, reports, artifacts, and severity thresholds into pull-request workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Lint one specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [SPEC_PATH] with Spectral. Identify the correct base ruleset, run linting, and summarize security findings with locations and fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one OpenAPI or AsyncAPI file

prompt_templates.title: Build a security ruleset
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Spectral ruleset for [API_TYPE]. Enforce HTTPS, authentication, safe parameters, standard errors, and [ORGANIZATION_REQUIREMENT]. Explain each rule.

prompt_templates.title: Triage lint findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the Spectral report at [REPORT_PATH]. Group findings by OWASP API category, remove false positives, prioritize fixes, and define verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design portfolio enforcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI policy for specifications under [SPEC_DIRECTORY]. Include pinned dependencies, immutable rules, failure handling, reports, exceptions, and phased severity enforcement.

output_examples.input: Review an OpenAPI specification for missing authentication and insecure servers.
output: High: Three operations do not declare a security requirement.
High: The production server uses HTTP instead of HTTPS.
Next step: Add the shared security scheme, apply it globally, and rerun Spectral.

output_examples.input: Summarize a Spectral report for an application security review.
output_examples.output: The report contains two errors and five warnings. Authentication and transport findings should block release; documentation warnings can enter the backlog.

output_examples.input: Plan CI enforcement for a large API portfolio.
output: Phase one reports errors and warnings without blocking.
Phase two blocks new error-level findings and records approved exceptions.
Phase three pins the ruleset and enforces the same policy across repositories.

best_practices: Pin Spectral, actions, rulesets, and downloaded tools to reviewed immutable versions.
Start with built-in rules, then add focused organizational checks with test fixtures.
Review findings manually and document justified exceptions with owners and expiration dates.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell or execute mutable downloaded scripts.
Do not suppress scanner failures without distinguishing tool errors from acceptable findings.
Do not treat specification linting as proof that runtime authentication and authorization are secure.

faq.question: Which specification formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and Arazzo through Spectral rulesets.

faq.question: Does this skill test a running API?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes API definition files and related governance rules.

faq.question: Can it create custom Spectral rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains JSONPath targets, built-in functions, custom functions, messages, and severity configuration.

faq.question: Can it run in continuous integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflow templates, but remote dependencies must be pinned before production use.

faq.question: Does every finding represent a vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. Spectral findings require context, false-positive review, and alignment with organizational policy.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Node.js, npm, and Spectral are primary requirements. Individual examples may also use Git, Docker, jq, or Python.
